assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 150,000 cache ops/s peak, 90% GET / 6% SET / 2% explicit invalidate / 2% write-through to the origin.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: 96% hit rate on the GET path. The 4% miss both reads the origin replica AND writes the value back to a primary shard, which is why `dbrep` and `cache` each carry visit_prob 0.04 on that flow.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Shard count (3 primaries + 3 replicas) is set by DATASET SIZE and failover topology, not by request rate - which is why the primaries sit at low utilisation. Sizing a Redis Cluster on rps alone would under-provision memory and cause evictions the engine does not model.

assumptions.subject: proxy
assumptions.statement: ~25,000 ops/s per 2-vCPU proxy instance. A hashing proxy is a byte-shuffler, so this is conservative for mcrouter/Envoy class software; it is the binding constraint in this design.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: The engine models steady-state throughput. A distributed cache's two most dangerous failure modes - a COLD cache after a flush (every GET becomes an origin read: 150k rps onto a single primary) and a hot-key shard imbalance - are not steady-state, so run them as explicit what-if scenarios rather than reading them off this baseline.

_library.summary: Sharded in-memory cache tier (Redis Cluster / memcached) fronting a slower system of record.
